proposal: The Mandate recommends that the SEC reduce burdens on small broker-dealers, including exempting privately held, non-custodial broker-dealers from the requirement to use a PCAOB-registered audit firm. It also recommends exempting peer-to-peer lending from federal and state securities laws and reducing the burden on Regulation CF debt securities.

status_summary: H.R. 10477, the Small Business Audit Correction Act of 2026 (Rep. Hill, introduced 2026-09-17, referred to House Financial Services), would exclude privately held, non-carrying broker-dealers in good standing from the Sarbanes-Oxley PCAOB audit provisions by amending the definitions in section 110 of that Act and direct the SEC to amend Rule 17a-5 to allow a standard GAAS audit. That is the audit exemption the Mandate describes, but it is a bill only. No SEC rule, proposal or exemptive order on broker-dealer audit requirements, peer-to-peer lending or Regulation CF debt was found.

timeline.event: H.R. 10477 was introduced to exempt privately held, non-carrying broker-dealers from the PCAOB audit requirement and was referred to the House Financial Services Committee.
